reference_action: Succulents overwatered with tiny frequent sips after moving to lower light: thoroughly soak only after full drying/wrinkling, increase light and raise plants above shading pot rims. OP confirms recovery.

sources.reason: Repot separately and provide a little sip, preserving the very watering pattern the reference corrects.
Deep watering only after bone-dry mix explicitly replaces shallow sips; gradual light adjustment also supplied.
0:29–0:46 let soil dry completely and soak/drain; 4:13 brighter window.
Gradual more sunlight and root drying before gritty repot.
Explains overwatering and dryness but treatment is heat shade or rot removal, not full-dry/soak regime or brighter light.

actions.action: Move small succulent to its own small pot
Water with a little sip after repotting
Separate large companion succulents into individual pots

resolved.reason: Misattributes trouble to competition and repeats sip watering rather than correcting frequency and light. This is ineffective but not necessarily actively harmful absent quantities.

harmfulness.reason: “Looks like might need a little sip” is poorly matched to repeated tiny watering. Separation itself may be safe, but failing to correct moisture and light can prolong stress.

specificity_accuracy.reason: Succulents are the correct group, but competition and never-watering address a different case. It ignores the explicit lower light and frequent watering history.

feasibility.reason: Separate pots are obtainable. Pot sizes, mix and the size/timing of the “sip” are insufficiently specified, and several plants require work.
